chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Haysam al-Ajali, Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Sa'iq, and Ali ibn Abdullah al-Varraq - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Hamzah ibn al-Qasim al-Alavi said: Al-Hasan ibn Matil al-Daqqaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdullah Ali ibn Muhammad al-Shazi narrated to us, from Ali ibn Yusuf, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say:
Whoever memorizes forty traditions from our traditions regarding the permissible and the forbidden, God will resurrect him on the Day of Judgment as a jurist, learned, and will not punish him.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for memorizing forty hadiths according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the spiritual and intellectual merit of preserving forty key traditions to ensure one's standing as a faqih (jurist) on the Day of Judgment. This number reflects the Shia tradition of 'thirty-six' plus four additional essential rulings, emphasizing the importance of mastering core legal knowledge for salvation. The promise of being spared from punishment underscores the direct link between scholarly diligence in understanding divine law and spiritual deliverance.
